institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, the proximity to my home city Copenhagen was an important factor, and then obviously the cultural and historical atmosphere of Paris. The prospect of learning French was also a plus, when choosing Paris

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university provided lots of info on the intro week and the semester. Actually, I think there may have been too much info, and that it eventually was treated more as spam messaging than useful info from Sciences Po. Concerning the city, it was easy to find your way around, and I had a generally positive experience with information sharing from public services such as transportation and stuff like that. The locals, teachers, neighbors etc. was all very helpful, and interested in providing the info necessary for settling in a new city.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a whole introductory week planned, which I didn't attend because it was a little too expensive for me. Additionally, there was a day, where students could meet the different communities and student organizations on campus, which gave a nice impression of the university. Furthermore, we received many mails daily on our student account on how and where to study.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are loads of studio apartments in Paris, and my impression is that many hosts are decent, but unfortunately there are a large number of scam apartments. I applied for the danish house in Cité Universitaire and was accepted. I can highly recommend applying for the Cité Universitaire. It is often cheaper than studios, you live with other students from all over the world in a community, and it is organized so you do not get ripped off in any way.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think Paris is a nice city to live in, and most areas feel safe to explore and walk through. The Cité Universitarie however feels like a university campus although the residents are a mix of all higher educations of Paris and many different nationalities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The website seemed old and the fact that it was a 'first past the post' process was quite stressful when choosing courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is an online course registration process, which opens in the morning and has a deadline 24 hours afterwards. You have to register manually and course by course along all other future exchange students online and then complete and close the registration file, when you are approved on the right amount of ECTS-points.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I am not aware.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the five courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready with a wishlist of courses when the registration process opens and have some second wishes ready if one of your main priorities gets full during the process. I believe it is a good idea to register when it opens and not hours afterwards, where many of the courses have been occupied.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The French education system seems focused on being elitist for the sake of being elitist. There seem to be a firm hierarchy between teachers and students, which makes critical questions hard to come through with because it is seen as a questioning of the teachers academic authority rather than a contribution to a reflected debate on a given subject.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Many of the courses did not have a syllabus and seemed more loosely structured. It sometimes reminded me of high school more than a university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Even though Sciences Po is considered an elite university/grande ecole it seemed more like high school and very focused on attendance, class participation and echoing teachers statements. It sometimes felt like the form 'elitist' was prioritized over substance and academic depth, which stands in contrast to the University of Copenhagen, where attendance and class participation are not part of your evaluation, but much more how you reflect and consider the syllabus texts and the way you use it to make sense of your surroundings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ASPO 25A11 Comparative Politics, DSPO 25A02 European integration and its challenges: the euro, migration and populism, DSPO 25A13 Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an insider's view (The), DAFF 25A18 Israeli Politics through Cinema, DAFF 25A89 Geopolitics and heritage dynamics in the Balkans

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend choosing the courses you find most interesting yourself on the syllabus. None of the courses I took were bad overall, but not recommendable in particular either.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected ones

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I researched before arriving in Paris, so I was not surprised of the expenses. However I found supermarket prices to be more expensive overall than I thought. I believe that many groceries can be bought cheaper in specialized vendors like greengrocers, butchers, bakeries etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not aware, because I wanted to explore the city rather than Sciences Po.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visiting museums, eating French food, exploring the city, going to libraries and so forth.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Paris is in many senses the European capital of cultural institutions and if you are an EU citizen between 18 and 26 years many of the state owned museums and attractions are free to visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy because most of the people I encountered were very helpful and kind to strangers like an exchange student as myself. I have been taught French in primary school and high school, so I was able to order in bars, cafés, restaurants and grocery stores without revealing my foreign nationality.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My impression is that local students like speaking French with each other and a good way to socializing and meeting those is to learn French on a more advanced level, than I was able to. If you are able to converse in French in an informal way, it is easier to approach local Parisians and students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language mostly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the French mentality in public spaces and their politeness towards each other. The way they use their city is quite elegant, and makes you want to participate in it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of work is much higher. There are a lot of class presentations, which feels like oral exams in front of other students. You are obliged to attend classes, if you are absent more than two times in a class during one semester you automatically fail the course.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I believe most has been said :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience another education system and analyzing, why it is built in that way. I treated all experiences as learnful ones, which I recommend future exchange students doing as well. It was also rewarding to live in Paris for such a long time, and not just to visit it as a tourist for a change.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of work and the education mentality at Sciences Po.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
